faq.q: Why do teenagers have a growth spurt?
faq.a: At puberty the body releases more growth hormone and sex hormones. Together they make the growth plates at the ends of long bones produce new bone much faster for a couple of years.

faq.q: Do you grow in your sleep?
faq.a: Much growth happens at night. Growth hormone is released in pulses, and the biggest pulses come during deep sleep, signalling bones and muscles to grow.
asks: Is it true children grow at night?

faq.q: Do boys and girls have growth spurts at the same time?
faq.a: No. Girls usually start their spurt around age 10 to 11, and boys around 12 to 13. Boys often end up taller partly because they grow for longer before the spurt.
asks: Why do girls grow taller first?

faq.q: How fast do children grow before the spurt?
faq.a: Between about age 3 and the start of puberty, most children grow fairly steadily, about 5 to 6 centimetres a year.
asks: How much do kids grow each year?
How tall do children get each year?

faq.q: Why do we stop growing taller?
faq.a: In the late teens, hormones cause the growth plates of cartilage near the ends of bones to turn completely into bone. Once they have closed, the bones cannot get longer.

facts: Most children grow roughly 5 to 6 centimetres a year between early childhood and puberty.
Growth hormone is released in pulses, with the largest usually during deep sleep.
Girls typically reach their peak growth rate about two years earlier than boys.

quiz.say: When does the body release the biggest pulses of growth hormone?
quiz.why: The largest pulses of growth hormone are released during deep sleep, so much growth happens at night.

wrong.1: Eating breakfast does not trigger the main growth hormone pulses.
wrong.2: Exercise can raise growth hormone a little, but the biggest pulses come in deep sleep.
